content.thinking:
I'm piecing together the postmortem facts: the spend-integrity check flagged mismatched shopper totals with the widest shortfall traced to an old purchase, and the deploy of 26f1d7e appears to be the culprit since record_purchase stopped updating the monthly total.

Both execution paths at that commit leave the month total unchanged, confirmed by actually-run code rather than an unexercised branch, so the root cause isn't hidden in untested logic. Since several downstream reads (monthly statement rendering, comparison-with-usual, average purchase, spend summary) all depend on that stale total, the visible symptom is that shoppers' monthly statements showed understated spend figures.

As for ruling out the earlier deploy P1: the alert AL1 dates the first harmed purchase at 09:14 Oct 19, which falls after P2's 09:13 timestamp, and no healthy metrics window spans the P1-to-onset period — so AL1's dating of first harm effectively rules out P1 as the cause, pointing to P2 instead.

AL1 directly, and D1 confirms the dropped line lives in P2's change, not P1's. T16 shows zero flag changes in the hour before onset, ruling that out too, and the derive-the-month flag path is identical across both commits at that point, so flag state can't be the cause. That leaves me checking whether record_purchase_deriving_the_month itself was actually unchanged at 4c810f2, since D1 only lists one hunk for that file.

Putting together the chain: shoppers' month-to-date totals fell short of what their purchases should show (per AL1, U3, U4), because purchases since onset were added to purchase history and lifetime total but never updated total_this_month_cents — confirmed in both code paths per S1 and AL1.

Revision 26f1d7e's record_purchase stopped setting total_this_month_cents, deployed at P2 and fully rolled out by T13, with P1, flag changes, and version splits all ruled out as causes. The deeper reason is that the change assumed the month figure would be derived on demand per its docstring, but every reader (U1, U2, U3, U6) still reads the stored field directly rather than deriving it — so the write path and read path fell out of sync.

That reaches a root cause. The remaining question is why this shipped with readers unchanged — that's a review/test gap, which becomes a contributing factor: CF-1 is that no test caught that record_purchase moving the month total was relied upon by readers (existing tests cover only the derive path, not record_purchase), so I should propose a test there to prevent recurrence. CF-2 is that the spend-integrity reconciliation only runs every few days, delaying detection, so increasing its frequency would help catch this faster.

CF-3 is that the alert never paged anyone — no on-call was linked despite routing config existing for it — so had it paged, someone would've acted sooner; I'll propose routing SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to page on-call as a process/detection fix.

CF-4 raises whether the derive path's identical latent bug counts as a contributing factor to this incident — since rolling back wouldn't fix that path, I'm weighing whether it actually would have stopped this particular incident or if it's really a separate, still-open risk.

I'm deciding the derive path belongs under still-at-risk rather than as a CF, since it wasn't shown to have caused this incident and AI-1 already addresses it; I'm also noting that removing field writes without checking for other readers is a related gap, but I'll fold that into CF-1 rather than creating a new factor. For action items, I'm distinguishing that rollback mitigates but doesn't repair, and proposing running the repair script against an account export before month-end to fix the corrupted totals.

I confirm deploying main would restore correct behavior since record_purchase there is already correct, so merging the draft PR just needs to make it to deploy. I'm also drafting a test verifying record_purchase updates total_this_month_cents for current-month purchases but not earlier-month ones, tied to CF-1, and considering a broader requirement that any change removing a field write must first confirm nothing still depends on reading it.

I'm separating this into two gaps: CF-1 covers the missing test that would catch an unmoved month total, while CF-2 covers the missing review step that would have checked remaining readers of the field before removing the write — distinct but related failures. For detection, I want to recommend running the spend-integrity check far more frequently than its current interval, ideally daily or triggered right after each purchase.

For the "went_well" section, I'm noting that Argus correctly placed the onset and identified the deploy, the Investigator read the relevant log shortly after the alert fired, Code-Fix drafted a PR promptly, and Argus ruled out flag changes by checking flag history rather than acting blind — all signs the system behaved as designed.

For "went_wrong," I'm flagging that the fault ran undetected from onset to alert, nobody got paged despite the severity, and a rollback was recommended but not actually taken.

For "got_lucky," there was no customer-facing impact since takings weren't affected—the monthly reads are statement-based rather than tied to checkout.

The real luck is timing: both onset and alert fell in the same calendar month, so totals could still be corrected from purchases flagged as in-progress before the month closed. Had the rollover happened first, the wrong statement likely would have already gone out, though that relies somewhat on how F1's in-current-month logic actually behaves.

But the underlying fix still hasn't landed everywhere — that revision still runs on every replica, so new purchases keep leaving the month total unmoved and the gap keeps growing while the already-wrong totals continue feeding monthly statements. Rolling back without addressing the derive path won't actually solve it.

I'm also second-guessing whether rollback would fully fix things, since the default record-purchase path there matches what's already broken. And I should flag as an assumption that the oldest affected purchase marks the true onset, even though the lookback window could hide an earlier start.

For the plain-language cause, I want to avoid naming components: a software update stopped each shopper's monthly running total from updating, while the pages that display it still show the old stored number. For the root cause, I'm pinning it to the revision that removed the update to the stored month-total field on the assumption it'd be derived on demand instead—except nothing was built to derive it, so every read path (statement, summary, reconciliation) still reads a stale stored value, and no write path moves it either.

Now I'm checking which replicas confirm this revision is live as of the dated instant, and drafting the user-facing symptom: month-to-date spend totals shown on the statement fall short of actual purchases, citing the integrity check's mismatch counts and worst-case gap. I'm also noting that the only identified contributing-factor fix addresses detection, not the underlying derive-path gap.

action_items.item: Rewrite the stored month total of each account the reconciliation check reports, setting it from that account's current-month purchases, and load the corrected accounts back into the store before the month rolls over (the draft PR's repair script only reports by default and does not load anything back).
Add a test that recording a current-month purchase through record_purchase moves total_this_month_cents, and that recording an earlier month's purchase leaves it alone.
Add a review check that a change which stops writing a stored account field also updates, or is blocked by, every place that still reads that field.
Run the spend-integrity reconciliation of month totals after every io-shop deploy, not only on its fixed schedule.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop to page the on-call engineer.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored spend totals for the month fell short of the purchases behind them. These are the figures the monthly statement shows. The spend-integrity check found {A1} of {A2} shopper totals that did not reconcile with their purchases. The widest was short by {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at {A4}.

Purchases recorded since the onset were added to the shopper's history and lifetime total, but the stored month total was left where it was. In the code that ran, both write paths build the account with only purchases and total_cents moved.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the first affected purchase at {A4}, after the deploy of 26f1d7e at {P2.1}, and D1 shows that 4c810f2's record_purchase still moved the month total.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider showed {T16.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T16.3} hour before the onset at {T16.4}.
A split between versions: all replicas ran the same revision.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, removed the update of total_this_month_cents from record_purchase, which had previously added the price of each current-month purchase. When T13 read the rollout at {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas were running that revision.

The change dropped the stored month total on the stated premise that the month figure would be derived from the purchases whenever it is needed. Nothing was changed to derive it: the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check still read account.total_this_month_cents directly. The field they read therefore stopped following new purchases.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update changed how purchases are written down so that each shopper's stored total for the month stopped going up, while the parts of the shop that show and check that total still read the stored figure.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that fails when recording a current-month purchase leaves the stored month total unmoved, so the removal in revision 26f1d7e reached production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The change would have failed before deploy and never reached shoppers' accounts.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No review step was seen that checks the readers of a stored field when a change stops writing it. The change dropped the write while the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check still read the field.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The mismatch between the dropped write and the remaining readers would have been caught in review, before deploy.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The only thing seen to check that month totals reconcile was the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The fault was therefore found only {alerted_after_the_onset} after the onset.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check run soon after the deploy would have found the mismatch while few accounts were wrong, and the wrong totals would have stopped spreading much sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so the rollback Argus recommended had no person called to carry it out.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been called to roll back as soon as the alert fired, cutting short the time new purchases kept being written wrong.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

got_lucky: The onset and the alert fell in the same calendar month. That means the wrong totals can still be rebuilt from purchases marked as falling in the current month, as long as that is done before the month rolls over.
went_well: The Investigator read the deployment diff of revision 26f1d7e {T12.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and the diff shows the dropped month-total update directly.
Argus checked the flag provider's history, ruling out a flag change as what set the incident off.
Code-Fix proposed a draft pull request with tests and a repair script, PR #356, {T21.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.

input.root_cause: Revision 26f1d7e stopped record_purchase from updating the stored month total (total_this_month_cents). Its docstring says the month figure would now be worked out from the purchase history whenever it is needed, but nothing was changed to do that. The monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check all still read the stored field, which no longer moves when a purchase is added. At that revision the other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, does not move it either, so no purchase written there updates the month total.
input.still_at_risk: Revision 26f1d7e was still running on every replica, so each new purchase would go on leaving the shopper's month total where it was, widening the gap behind what the monthly statement shows; the totals already written wrong stayed wrong; and the other write path in the same file leaves the month total unmoved even on main and in the revision a rollback would restore, so it could do the same thing again if it were used.
input.symptom: Shoppers' spend totals for the month fell short of what they had bought
